component: nginx + ASGI/net-http/FrankenPHP servers keeping '#' in the request-target
version: nginx 1.30.7-alpine; fastapi uvicorn/h11; go-chi Go net/http; laravel FrankenPHP 1.14.0
title: Fragment nested-route substitution: a DPoP proof accepted for one op executes an adjacent nested op
mechanism: nginx forwards the raw '#...' request-target upstream; the server keeps '#...' in the request path and routes on it; the RFC 9449/3986 verifier drops the fragment and binds the base op. A nested same-method route (GET /accounts/{id}/statements, DELETE /accounts/{id}/statements/{sid}) catches the kept suffix.
where_observed: nginx x {fastapi,go-chi,laravel}, default profile, override off+on (6 topologies); getAccount->getStatements (S2), deleteAccount->deleteStatement (S1)
practical_impact: Operation binding broken (res>1). Target resource id is the mangled 'acc-alice-1#' so the attacker cannot pick the resource, but the executed operation is not the authorised one.
notes: Composed finding. The '#'-keeping parser is the W9 F1 class (uvicorn h11); this extends it from an id suffix (W9 RC6) to a different operation via the nested route. Check upstream trackers (uvicorn/h11, Go net/http, FrankenPHP/Caddy, nginx) before any disclosure.

component: uvicorn/h11 (and Go net/http, FrankenPHP) accepting '#' in the request-target
version: fastapi uvicorn/h11; go-chi net/http; laravel FrankenPHP 1.14.0
title: HTTP server keeps '#' and everything after it inside request.url.path
mechanism: Per RFC 3986 the '#' begins a fragment and is not part of the request-target; these servers keep it in the path, so a proxy that forwards the raw byte lets it reach routing.
practical_impact: Enables F1 and the id-suffix variant (W9 RC6).
notes: Same root component as W9 F1 (uvicorn h11). Re-confirmed on go-chi and laravel/FrankenPHP in this round.

component: RFC-3986 verifier vs catch-all route dot-segment disagreement
title: Catch-all path captures a no-op dot segment the verifier normalised away
mechanism: The verifier removes './' and decodes '%2e' (RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.3) and binds the canonical htu; the gateway forwards raw; the catch-all route keeps the literal segment.
where_observed: both gateways x {fastapi,express,django,go-chi,spring,rails,laravel}, default profile, override off+on
practical_impact: Practically low: only the no-op './' / '%2e/' passes; every '..'/encoded-slash/pct2f traversal is denied by the verifier (htu_mismatch). No distinct file, route or owner is reachable.
notes: Realises W9 section 5 latent L1 (dot segments) as an executed request, because the catch-all does not 404. aspnet normalises './' in routing and is unaffected.

version: express method-override 3.0.0; laravel Symfony _method; rails Rack::MethodOverride; aspnet UseHttpMethodOverride; django-method-override 1.0.4; go-chi gorilla HTTPMethodOverrideHandler; spring HiddenHttpMethodFilter; fastapi HTTPMethodOverrideASGI
title: A leaked POST proof executes PUT/DELETE via method-override on a path shared by POST and PUT/DELETE
mechanism: With a POST route sharing /accounts/{id} with PUT/DELETE, the override middleware rewrites the method after the verifier's (raw) view is taken, so postAccount's proof routes to updateAccount/deleteAccount.
where_observed: all 8 frameworks, OVERRIDE=on; Rails (full stack) and Laravel ship it on by default
practical_impact: S1 state change (POST authorisation becomes DELETE/PUT).
notes: By-design G1 (method not covered by the proof; CONTRACT section 7). Reported as the task's POST-override deliverable, not as a new vuln. Defence D-A (VERIFY_MODE=origin-routed) stops it.

component: FastAPI HTTPMethodOverrideASGI honours override on any base method
title: X-HTTP-Method-Override honoured on GET/any method (Flask pattern)
mechanism: Unlike the POST-only middlewares, the ASGI override acts on any method, so a GET proof -> DELETE.
notes: Config-dependent; off by default; do not present as a FastAPI default.
